questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The cost of a territorial state

stimulus.body: Der folgende Auszug dient der Überprüfung des Verständnisses dieser Form. «A territorial state costs more due to permanent institutions.» Von vier Antworten passt allein diejenige, die sich aus dem Text ergibt.

questions.stem: Mit «Compare costs of state types / Permanent institutions raise cost. / The cost of a territorial state» im Blick, welche Option entspricht dem Auszug?

options.text: Neither type has any administrative cost
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

options.text: A personal union always costs more in every case
Both cost exactly the same by definition
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

options.text: A territorial state costs more due to permanent institutions

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: territorial states carry permanent institutions and thus higher costs. On that basis "A territorial state costs more due to permanent institutions" is the supported choice. Option A ("Neither type has any administrative cost") fails because it substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the cost of a territorial state; Option B ("A personal union always costs more in every case") fails because it overgeneralises union costs; Option C ("Both cost exactly the same by definition") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles the cost of a territorial state.
questions.hint: Permanent institutions raise cost.

questions.stem: Wendet man «Contrast 1804 equality with later rights / Legal and merit-based only. / The equality established in 1804» auf den Text an, welche Option ist begründet?

options.text: 1804 abolished all economic inequality
1804 already included universal suffrage
1804 equality was legal, not political or social
1804 ended all class distinctions immediately

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the code's equality was legal and merit-based. On that basis "1804 equality was legal, not political or social" is the supported choice. Option A ("1804 abolished all economic inequality") fails because it overstates legal equality; Option B ("1804 already included universal suffrage") fails because it projects later demands backward; Option D ("1804 ended all class distinctions immediately") fails because it confuses legal with social equality.
questions.hint: Legal and merit-based only.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The order of two past events

stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: «The press could not cause an earlier founding.» A text places the founding of a university in 1386 and a printing press in 1455, yet a commentator claims the press caused the university's founding. Der folgende Auszug dient der Überprüfung des Verständnisses dieser Form. Von vier Antworten passt allein diejenige, die sich aus dem Text ergibt.

questions.stem: Der Auszug wird an «Reject anachronism / Later event cannot cause earlier one. / The order of two past events» geprüt. Welche Antwort bleibt bestehen?

options.text: The university was founded after the press
options.misconception: selects "The university was founded after the press" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: The dates are interchangeable
options.misconception: treats "The dates are interchangeable" as if it followed from the evidence

options.text: The press could not cause an earlier founding
Both events happened in the same decade

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the dates are fixed and not interchangeable or simultaneous. On that basis "The press could not cause an earlier founding" is the supported choice. Option A ("The university was founded after the press") fails because it selects "The university was founded after the press" where the order of two past events requires a different condition; Option B ("The dates are interchangeable") fails because it treats "The dates are interchangeable" as if it followed from the evidence; Option D ("Both events happened in the same decade") fails because it collapses distinct dates.
questions.hint: Later event cannot cause earlier one.
